title: Migraine prevention (adult)
subject: neurology
setting: Primary care, neurology and headache clinic
summary: Offer prevention for 4 or more migraine days a month or disabling migraine; choose propranolol, amitriptyline, topiramate (not in pregnancy or without highly effective contraception), candesartan or a CGRP-targeted drug by comorbidity and access, treat medication overuse, and judge response after 8 to 12 weeks at target dose.

sections.title: Who needs prevention
items: Offer prevention (AAN/AHS 2026) for 4 or more migraine days a month, 4 or more moderate to severe headache days a month, or migraine that substantially affects work or daily life.
Also consider prevention when acute treatments are contraindicated, ineffective or being overused.
Chronic migraine: headache on 15 or more days a month for more than 3 months, with migraine features on at least 8 of those days.
Use a headache diary to count migraine days and acute-medication days and to measure response.
Recheck for red flags if the pattern changes (see Acute migraine attack (adult)), and look for medication overuse headache.

sections.title: Medication overuse headache
items: Suspect it if headache developed or worsened while taking triptans, opioids, ergots or combination analgesics on 10 or more days a month, or simple analgesics on 15 or more days a month, for 3 months or more.
Treatment is withdrawal: stop all overused acute medicines abruptly for at least 1 month (NICE); withdraw opioids gradually, with specialist input if needed.
Warn that headache may worsen before it improves; start prevention at the same time where appropriate; review 4 to 8 weeks after withdrawal.

sections.title: Choosing a preventive
items: Choose by comorbidity, pregnancy potential, side effects, cost and access. AAN/AHS 2026 (level B): atogepant, CGRP monoclonal antibodies, propranolol, topiramate or valproate; add onabotulinumtoxinA for chronic migraine.
NICE: consider propranolol, topiramate or amitriptyline first. Candesartan is an evidence-based alternative (SIGN, AHS); flunarizine is used where available (SIGN).
Propranolol: good with hypertension, anxiety or tremor; avoid in asthma, bradycardia and heart block; use caution with depression because of overdose toxicity (NICE).
Amitriptyline: good with insomnia, depression or coexisting tension-type headache; avoid with conduction disease, glaucoma or urinary retention; toxic in overdose.

Topiramate: must not be used in pregnancy; women who could become pregnant need the Pregnancy Prevention Programme with highly effective contraception (topiramate can reduce hormonal contraceptive effect). Avoid with kidney stones or glaucoma.
Valproate: in the UK only for adults over 55 (SIGN, MHRA); never for women who could become pregnant. Do not use gabapentin for prevention (NICE).

sections.title: CGRP-targeted and specialist options
items: CGRP monoclonal antibodies (erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, eptinezumab) and gepants (atogepant, rimegepant) are first-line options in the AHS 2024 position and AAN/AHS 2026 guideline; NICE funds them only after at least 3 preventives have failed or are unsuitable.

Avoid CGRP monoclonal antibodies in pregnancy and breastfeeding (SIGN advises a 6-month washout before trying to conceive); weigh risks in high ischaemic cardiovascular risk. Erenumab can cause constipation and raise blood pressure.
Chronic migraine after 3 failed preventives: onabotulinumtoxinA every 12 weeks in a headache service, once medication overuse is addressed.
Riboflavin 400 mg once daily may reduce migraine frequency for some people (NICE).
Predictable menstrual migraine: frovatriptan 2.5 mg twice daily or zolmitriptan 2.5 mg two or three times daily from 2 days before until 3 days after bleeding starts.

sections.title: Review
items: Start low and increase slowly; judge effect after 8 to 12 weeks at the target or maximum tolerated dose (24 weeks for onabotulinumtoxinA).
Aim for a 50% or greater fall in migraine days, or a clear improvement in disability (MIDAS or HIT-6).
Stop CGRP drugs at 12 weeks if migraine frequency has not fallen by at least 50% in episodic or 30% in chronic migraine (NICE).
Review the need for continuing prevention 3 to 6 months after starting (NICE); if migraine is well controlled, discuss a gradual taper.
Failure of one class does not predict failure of another; try a different class.

sections.title: Pregnancy, contraception and India
items: Planning pregnancy or pregnant: seek specialist advice; avoid valproate, topiramate, candesartan, flunarizine, CGRP monoclonal antibodies and gepants. If prevention is essential, specialist options include a beta blocker such as propranolol or metoprolol (AAN/AHS 2026).
Migraine with aura: do not routinely offer combined hormonal contraceptives (NICE).
India: flunarizine, propranolol, amitriptyline and topiramate are inexpensive and widely used; access to CGRP-targeted drugs is limited by availability and cost.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Stopping a preventive after 2 to 3 weeks at a low dose, before it could work.
Missing medication overuse, which makes preventives less effective.
Prescribing topiramate or valproate to a woman who could become pregnant without the Pregnancy Prevention Programme.
Giving propranolol to someone with asthma, or large quantities to someone with depression.
Using opioids or codeine combinations for migraine.

drugs.name: Propranolol
drugs.dose: 40 mg orally two or three times daily; maintenance 80 to 160 mg daily (divided, or modified-release once daily)
drugs.notes: Avoid in asthma, bradycardia, heart block and uncontrolled heart failure. Dangerous in overdose.

drugs.name: Amitriptyline
drugs.dose: 10 mg orally at night, increased gradually; usual 25 to 75 mg at night (SIGN range 25 to 150 mg)
drugs.notes: Sedation, dry mouth, constipation, weight gain; avoid with conduction disease. Toxic in overdose.

drugs.name: Topiramate
drugs.dose: 25 mg at night for 1 week, then increase by 25 mg weekly to 50 mg twice daily (100 mg daily); SIGN range 50 to 100 mg daily
drugs.notes: Paraesthesia, cognitive slowing, weight loss, kidney stones, acute angle-closure glaucoma. Pregnancy Prevention Programme.

drugs.name: Candesartan
drugs.notes: Check blood pressure, renal function and potassium. Avoid in pregnancy and breastfeeding.

drugs.name: Flunarizine
drugs.notes: Weight gain, sedation, depression, parkinsonism (especially older adults). Avoid in depression, parkinsonism and pregnancy. Not licensed in the UK or USA.

drugs.name: Erenumab
drugs.dose: 70 mg SC every month; some need 140 mg monthly (NICE funds 140 mg)
drugs.notes: Constipation, hypertension. Stop at 12 weeks if response is inadequate.

drugs.name: Fremanezumab
drugs.dose: 225 mg SC monthly, or 675 mg SC every 3 months

drugs.name: Galcanezumab
drugs.dose: 240 mg SC loading dose, then 120 mg SC monthly

drugs.name: Atogepant
drugs.notes: Nausea, constipation. Lower doses with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or severe renal impairment. Avoid in pregnancy.
